translationRepairs: From Kaiyuan to Xiande, fifty-three years passed—and through them the realm saw five dynasties.
From Kaiping to Xiande, fifty-three years passed—and through them the realm saw five dynasties.
Chinese 開平 is the Later Liang Kaiping era, not Kaiyuan (開元).
From the Kaiyuan era through Xiande, fifty-three years in all—and through that span the realm knew five dynasties.
From the Kaiping era through Xiande, fifty-three years in all—and through that span the realm knew five dynasties.
Chinese 開平 is Kaiping, not Kaiyuan.

The Deposed Emperor posthumously made Jinzong General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
The Chu Emperor posthumously made Jinzong General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
Chinese 出帝 is the Jin Chu Emperor, not the Deposed Emperor (廢帝/湣帝).
The Deposed Emperor posthumously made Jinzong General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
The Chu Emperor posthumously made Jinzong General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard.
Chinese 出帝 is the Jin Chu Emperor, not the Deposed Emperor.
Then Wang Chongzhi went with Cheng as deputy; Mo, Cheng, and the rest offered six Huai prefectures and a million a year in tribute.
Then he sent Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi as deputy to Cheng with a memorial; Mo, Cheng, and the rest offered six Huai prefectures and a million a year in tribute.
Chinese 王崇質副晟 means Chongzhi was Cheng’s deputy, not that Cheng was the deputy.

Then he sent Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi with Cheng as deputy with a memorial; Mo, Cheng, and the rest all said Jing would cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai and pay a million a year to support the army.

Then he sent Minister of Rites Wang Chongzhi as Cheng’s deputy with a memorial; Mo, Cheng, and the rest all said Jing would cede the six prefectures of Shou, Hao, Si, Chu, Guang, and Hai and pay a million a year to support the army.
Chinese 副晟 makes Wang Chongzhi the deputy accompanying Cheng; the literal reverses who is deputy.

Mo and the rest saw Shizong’s martial brilliance was no match for Jing and the army was mighty and Shouchun near peril; they said, “We beg Your Majesty grant us five days’ reprieve to return and bring Jing’s memorial offering all north-of-the-Huai prefectures."

Mo and the rest saw Shizong’s martial brilliance was beyond Jing’s matching and the army was mighty and Shouchun near peril; they said, “We beg Your Majesty grant us five days’ reprieve to return and bring Jing’s memorial offering all north-of-the-Huai prefectures."
Chinese 世宗英武非景敵 means Jing was no match for Shizong; the literal reverses the comparison.
Jing had ceded north Huai and sent Mo back; hearing Cheng was dead, he too posthumously made him Duke of Lu.
Jing had ceded land north of the Yangzi and sent Mo back; hearing Cheng was dead, he too posthumously made him Duke of Lu.
Chinese 江北 is north of the Yangzi, not the Huai; the idiomatic mistranslates the ceded region.
